name: Laser Flow
description: WebGL2 shader background of a vertical laser beam that drops in, hits a surface and spills glowing light, fog, streaks and dust across it, with a cursor-following lens that can reveal an image.
contents: Full-size container with a single WebGL2 canvas rendering the beam, spill, fog, dust and streaks
Optional surface element the beam lands on, measured from surfaceRef
Optional reveal image shown as light near the cursor
behavior: Beam drops from the top with a spring bloom intro, then settles into a continuous animation
Light spills and flows along the top edge of the surface, with fog, drifting dust and twinkling sparks
Cursor lens follows the pointer with spring motion, brightens the glow and reveals the image
Renders only while visible in the viewport and the tab is active
Skips the intro and stops motion when the user prefers reduced motion
editableByProps: Beam horizontal position, width, flare, spread, intensity and color
Fog, dust, streaks, dots, pulse, animation speed and noise seed
Surface the beam lands on through surfaceRef, or a fallback surface level
Cursor interaction, reveal image, radius and opacity
Intro on or off, dark or light theme, pause, pixel ratio, extra class and div attributes

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the hue and saturation offsets of the glow layers
Change the intro duration or drop speed
Change the beam look, spill shapes or fog logic

fixed: Requires WebGL2; renders nothing if it is unavailable
Fills its parent (h-full w-full), so the parent needs a defined size
Container is pointer-events-none, so it never captures clicks
Listens to window pointermove and document pointerleave for the cursor lens, cleaned up on unmount
Render resolution is capped at 2048px on the longest side and DPR at 2
Reveal image is loaded with crossOrigin anonymous, so it needs CORS headers
Heavy full-screen fragment shader; may be slow on low-end mobile GPUs
Beam color is derived by hue and saturation shifts from color, so palette is fixed to that scheme
